h1: We hire people who build things and answer the phone.
heroSubhead: VDS is a hardware company with a 24/7 monitoring operation. The work is hands-on, the customers are real, and the chain of command is short. Open roles are listed below. Speculative resumes welcome.

## What it is like to work here

VDS is small enough that you will meet the founders in your first week and large enough that you will not be doing three jobs at once. Headcount is in the 25–50 range. Decisions get made fast. Customer problems get answered fast. The work is operational, not theoretical.

Engineering ships firmware to units in the field — the kind that get vandalized, baked in 105°F sun, and rained on. Operations runs a 24/7 SOC with measurable response time targets. Sales talks to GCs, facility managers, and dealers who will tell you in plain language whether the product solves their problem. Manufacturing assembles units in Pikesville and inspects every chassis before it ships.

What we hire for, in order:
1. Will the person do the work
2. Can the person be trusted with a customer relationship
3. Does the person have the specific skills the role requires

That order is intentional.

## Compensation and benefits

- Competitive base salary, calibrated to role and experience
- Health, dental, and vision insurance (employer-contributing)
- 401(k) with company match after 6 months
- Paid time off, paid holidays, and paid parental leave
- Tools, equipment, and certifications relevant to the role, fully reimbursed
- Continuing education stipend for technical certifications

## Open roles {#open-roles}

### Hardware Assembly Technician
**Location:** Pikesville, MD (on-site)
**Type:** Full-time

Build, test, and inspect VDS mobile surveillance units on the Pikesville assembly line. Solar arrays, battery banks, camera modules, control electronics, cellular uplinks, and chassis. Read a wiring diagram, follow a build sequence, use a torque wrench, document a build sheet.

**What we need:**
- 2+ years assembly, electromechanical, or electrical work
- Comfortable with hand tools, basic soldering, and 12V/24V DC wiring
- Able to read schematics and follow written build procedures
- Detail-oriented; documents and labels work as it goes
- Lift 50 lbs, work in a shop environment with PPE

**What is nice to have:**
- Background in solar installation, RV/marine electrical, or fleet vehicle build-out
- Familiarity with low-voltage IP camera systems

**To apply:** Email resume to careers@visiondetectionsystems.com with subject "Hardware Assembly Technician."

### Administrative Coordinator
**Location:** Pikesville, MD (on-site)
**Type:** Full-time

Keep the operations side of VDS running. Customer billing coordination, vendor invoice processing, shipping coordination with the SOC and dealer channel, executive scheduling support, office logistics. This is the role where, if you do it well, the entire company runs better.

**What we need:**
- 3+ years administrative or operations coordination experience
- Excellent written communication and follow-through
- Comfortable with QuickBooks, Google Workspace, and a ticketing system (we use HubSpot)
- Ability to keep confidential information confidential
- Self-directed; you will not be micromanaged

**What is nice to have:**
- Background in B2B services, security industry, construction services, or fleet operations
- Notary commission

**To apply:** Email resume to careers@visiondetectionsystems.com with subject "Administrative Coordinator."

### Other roles — speculative resumes welcome

We hire continuously across:

- **Security Operations Center operators** — 24/7 shifts, US-staffed only, paid training
- **Firmware and embedded engineering** — Linux on edge devices, C/C++, low-power systems
- **Cloud platform engineering** — AWS, React, Node.js, video pipelines at scale
- **Field service technicians** — regional, US-based, drive a service truck, fix what is in the field
- **Account executives and dealer channel managers** — security industry experience preferred
- **Customer success managers** — own enterprise renewals and expansion

If your background fits one of these and there is no posted role, send a resume with the area of interest in the subject line. We respond within 5 business days.

## How hiring works

1. Resume submission via email
2. 30-minute phone screen with the hiring manager
3. 45–60 minute role-specific interview (technical, operational, or scenario-based)
4. On-site visit to Pikesville for final-round candidates (travel reimbursed for out-of-area candidates)
5. Reference check and offer

We do not run multi-day interview loops. We do not give homework assignments longer than 2 hours. We give a decision within one week of the final interview.

## What we will not do

- We do not hire for unposted roles through recruiters without a prior agreement
- We do not negotiate compensation through agencies on roles we did not retain them for
- We do not accept resumes for roles where you did not personally submit
- We do not require non-compete agreements as a condition of employment

faq.q: Do you offer remote work?
faq.a: SOC operators are on-site at the monitoring facility. Hardware assembly and field service are on-site. Engineering and some operations roles are hybrid with 2 days on-site per week.

faq.q: Do you sponsor visas?
faq.a: For some senior engineering roles, yes. State your work authorization status in your initial email; we will be direct about feasibility.

faq.q: How fast do you hire?
faq.a: From resume to offer is typically 2-3 weeks for posted roles. SOC operator hiring is faster — 7-10 days from screen to start date.

faq.q: Will I hear back if I am not selected?
faq.a: Yes. Every applicant who reaches the phone screen gets a closing email.

h1: Close the three gaps in site security.
heroSubhead: Most sites are protected by a fence, a sign, and a hope. We build the layer between those and the actual response.
heroStats: Founded 2017 · 500+ deployments · 30+ states · 7 years of field data
body:
## Why VDS exists

In 2017, the founders walked job sites where the security plan was a guard in a folding chair, a camera nobody was watching, and a sign that said "Premises Under Surveillance." When something happened — copper theft, equipment vandalism, an after-hours break-in — the response time averaged 18 to 40 minutes. By then the trailer was empty.

That gap between "we have cameras" and "someone is actually doing something about this right now" is the problem we set out to fix.

## The three gaps

We started VDS because site security in the field has three structural failures, and most vendors only address one.

**1. Cost.** Permanent fiber-trenched, hardwired surveillance costs $40K–$120K per acre and takes weeks to install. For a 90-day construction project or a seasonal yard, that math never works. Sites stay uncovered, and losses get written into the budget as "shrinkage."

**2. Blind spots.** Fixed cameras see a fence line. They do not see the lot, the staging area, the back row of equipment, or the access road. Guards see one quadrant at a time. Most sites are 60–80% un-monitored at any given moment.

**3. Response time.** Even when something is captured on camera, the average time from event to dispatched response is 18+ minutes industry-wide. Footage is great for insurance. It is not security.

## What we built

VDS is built as a manufacturer, not a reseller. We assemble our hardware in Pikesville, MD — Sky Guard MSU, Swift Deploy, Boundary Guard Pro, solar camera poles, guard booths, cooling stations, light trailers. We run the cloud VMS (AI VisionStream) on AWS. We staff our own 24/7 SOC in the US.

That stack matters because the three gaps are connected. You cannot fix response time if your camera vendor, your cloud vendor, and your monitoring vendor are three different companies pointing at each other. You cannot guarantee NDAA compliance if you are reselling whatever the distributor had in stock. You cannot keep pricing predictable if every layer is marked up by someone else.

So we own the layers. One number to call. One company accountable for the outcome.

## What "integrated mobile security infrastructure" actually means

It means the camera, the power source, the chassis, the network, the VMS, and the human watching the screen at 3 AM all answer to the same company. It means a Sky Guard MSU deployed in Arizona and one deployed in Maine pull data into the same platform, get monitored by the same SOC, and run on the same audit log. It means when a customer asks "who is watching this site right now," the answer is a name, not a vendor chain.

## The commitments

These are the things we do not compromise on, regardless of price pressure or growth pressure.

- **Manufacturer, not reseller.** We assemble. We integrate. We program. We own the warranty.
- **Genuine NDAA Section 889.** Every camera, every component — not "NDAA-compatible" marketing language.
- **In-house US SOC.** Not contracted offshore. <60s escalation, 97% false alarm reduction.
- **Your data is yours.** US-only data residency, TLS 1.3 / AES-256, 12-month audit log, no third-party data sale, ever.
- **Camera-agnostic platform.** If a customer has existing cameras that meet our compliance baseline, they integrate. We do not lock customers into our hardware.

## Where we are going

7 years of field data tells us where the next gaps are: edge AI for specific threat classes, faster deploy times, lower watts-per-channel, and tighter integration with the responders who actually show up. That is the roadmap. The mission has not changed: close the three gaps, and be the company you can actually call.

faq.q: Is VDS a security guard company?
faq.a: No. We build the mobile security infrastructure — hardware, cloud VMS, and 24/7 SOC monitoring — that makes guard services either unnecessary or far more effective. Our SOC handles detection and escalation; on-site response is dispatched through your existing guard provider or local law enforcement.

faq.q: Why does manufacturing in the US matter for security?
faq.a: NDAA Section 889 compliance is only meaningful if you can trace components. When you assemble in-house, you control the bill of materials, the firmware, and the supply chain. Resellers cannot make that guarantee — they ship what their distributors ship.

faq.q: How is VDS different from a camera vendor or a VMS vendor?
faq.a: Camera vendors sell you cameras. VMS vendors sell you software. Guard companies sell you hours. We are the only company that owns all three layers — and that's the only way to fix response time end-to-end.

faq.q: Where are you headquartered?
faq.a: Pikesville, Maryland. Founded 2017. All hardware is assembled here. The SOC is staffed in the US.

VDS hardware and AI VisionStream are fully NDAA Section 889 compliant. Written compliance documentation available for all federal, state, and regulated procurement programs.

## What Is NDAA Section 889?

The National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) Section 889 was enacted as part of the 2019 National Defense Authorization Act to address national security concerns regarding telecommunications and video surveillance equipment. Section 889 prohibits federal agencies from procuring or using equipment and services from companies that utilize covered telecommunications or video surveillance equipment from five specific manufacturers: Huawei Technologies, ZTE Corporation, Hytera Communications, Hangzhou Hikvision, and Dahua Technology.

The law contains two critical parts: Part A prevents federal agencies from directly purchasing equipment from these restricted manufacturers, while Part B extends the prohibition to federal contractors, preventing them from using this equipment anywhere in their operations. Part B became effective August 13, 2020, and applies to any organization seeking federal contracts or grants.

Beyond federal procurement, NDAA Section 889 compliance requirements have extended to state and local government agencies receiving federal funding, creating widespread impact across public sector surveillance and security programs. Many regulated industries now require NDAA compliance as a standard procurement criterion.

## Who NDAA Section 889 Affects

NDAA Section 889 compliance requirements extend across multiple sectors and procurement programs:

  • Federal Agencies — All executive departments including DOD, DHS, GSA, and their procurement programs must verify contractor compliance before award
  • State and Local Government — Agencies receiving federal funding through grants, cooperative agreements, or federal program participation must demonstrate compliance
  • Federal Contractors and Subcontractors — Any organization bidding on federal contracts must certify that they do not use restricted equipment in their operations
  • Critical Infrastructure Operators — Power, water, transportation, and communication networks often require NDAA compliance for security system procurements
  • Public Safety Agencies — Law enforcement, emergency management, and public safety organizations receiving federal grants must meet compliance standards
  • Regulated Procurement Programs — GSA schedule, cooperative purchasing agreements, and state contract vehicles increasingly require NDAA compliance certification
## Risks of Non-Compliance

Organizations that fail to meet NDAA Section 889 requirements face significant procurement and operational consequences. Contract disqualification represents the most immediate risk — procurement teams cannot award contracts to vendors who cannot certify compliance, regardless of technical capabilities or pricing advantages.

Federal contractors face suspension or debarment from all federal contracting opportunities if found using restricted equipment. The Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) requires contractors to remove any covered equipment from their systems, creating costly operational disruption and potential security gaps during transition periods.

Criminal penalties apply to organizations that provide false certifications regarding their compliance status. Procurement audits increasingly require component-level documentation to verify compliance claims, making inadequate due diligence a significant legal and business risk.

Beyond regulatory consequences, non-compliant security systems may require complete replacement if discovered during contract performance, creating budget overruns and coverage gaps that expose facilities to security incidents during system transitions.

## How VDS Meets NDAA Section 889 ### Hardware Supply Chain

VDS maintains a fully audited hardware supply chain free from all Section 889-restricted manufacturers. Our mobile surveillance trailers, solar camera poles, and fixed surveillance units contain no components from Huawei, ZTE, Hikvision, Dahua, or Hytera. Written attestation letters documenting supply chain compliance are available on request for all procurement programs.

Camera sensors, video processors, cellular modems, and connectivity modules are sourced exclusively from compliant suppliers with documented component traceability. All surveillance hardware is assembled in our Maryland facility under controlled manufacturing processes that maintain compliance integrity throughout production and deployment.

### AI VisionStream Software Platform

The AI VisionStream platform operates on Amazon Web Services (AWS) infrastructure with no restricted software manufacturers in the technology stack. Video analytics, cloud storage, user management, and API integrations utilize only compliant software libraries and services. AWS GovCloud deployment options are available for highest-classification government installations requiring additional security controls.

All software development, cloud hosting, and data processing occurs within compliant infrastructure, ensuring that video data, AI processing, and user access management meet Section 889 requirements from capture through evidence export.

### Documentation Package

VDS procurement support includes comprehensive compliance documentation for federal, state, and regulated purchasing programs. Our documentation package provides written NDAA Section 889 compliance attestation letters signed by executive management, component-level supply chain documentation upon request, and direct procurement support for GSA schedule, cooperative purchasing, and state contract vehicle processes.

Direct manufacturer relationships eliminate third-party channel partner compliance complexity, providing procurement teams with clear accountability and documentation trails. Most compliance packages are delivered within 48 hours of request, supporting tight procurement timelines and proposal deadlines.

## Federal and State Procurement Programs

VDS actively participates in federal and state procurement programs with full NDAA compliance documentation. Our GSA schedule participation provides federal agencies with pre-vetted pricing and compliance verification, streamlining procurement processes for mobile surveillance trailers and monitoring services.

State contract vehicles and cooperative purchasing agreements receive the same compliance documentation and pricing transparency, enabling state and local agencies to leverage federal-level procurement efficiency while meeting their own compliance requirements. Procurement teams receive dedicated support for compliance questions, technical specifications, and program requirements throughout the evaluation and award process.

Most procurement inquiries receive comprehensive compliance packages and technical proposals within 48 hours, supporting aggressive procurement timelines and budget cycles. Direct manufacturer engagement eliminates reseller markups and compliance uncertainties common in security system procurements.

## Ongoing Compliance Monitoring

VDS maintains continuous monitoring of supply chain compliance through quarterly supplier audits and component traceability reviews. Supply chain changes undergo compliance verification before implementation, ensuring that hardware updates, software releases, and service modifications maintain Section 889 compliance throughout product lifecycles.

Regulatory updates and guidance changes are tracked through federal procurement channels, with compliance documentation updated to reflect current requirements. This proactive approach ensures that existing deployments and new installations continue meeting compliance standards as regulations evolve.

Client compliance support extends beyond initial procurement to include compliance verification for contract renewals, system expansions, and regulatory audits. Written compliance confirmations are available throughout service relationships to support ongoing procurement and compliance requirements.

## NDAA Compliance FAQ ### What is NDAA Section 889?

NDAA Section 889 is federal legislation that prohibits government agencies and federal contractors from using telecommunications and video surveillance equipment from five specific manufacturers: Huawei, ZTE, Hikvision, Dahua, and Hytera. The law applies to federal agencies directly and extends to contractors, subcontractors, and organizations receiving federal funding.

### Which surveillance camera brands are banned under NDAA Section 889?

Section 889 specifically restricts equipment from Hangzhou Hikvision Digital Technology and Dahua Technology Company, along with telecommunications equipment from Huawei Technologies, ZTE Corporation, and Hytera Communications Corporation. The restriction applies to equipment manufactured by these companies or containing their components.

### Does NDAA compliance apply to state and local government?

Yes, NDAA Section 889 applies to state and local government agencies that receive federal funding through grants, cooperative agreements, or federal program participation. Many state procurement programs now require NDAA compliance regardless of federal funding to maintain consistent security standards across government operations.

### How do I verify that security equipment is NDAA compliant?

Request written compliance attestation letters from manufacturers documenting that their hardware and software contain no components from restricted manufacturers. Verify that suppliers can provide component-level documentation and maintain compliant supply chains. Work directly with manufacturers rather than resellers to ensure compliance accountability.

### Can VDS provide written NDAA compliance documentation for procurement?

Yes, VDS provides comprehensive NDAA Section 889 compliance documentation including signed attestation letters, component-level supply chain documentation, and procurement support for federal, state, and cooperative purchasing programs. Most compliance packages are delivered within 48 hours of request.

## Procurement Support and Documentation

For procurement teams requiring NDAA compliance verification and documentation, VDS provides direct manufacturer support throughout the evaluation and procurement process. Our compliance team works with federal agencies, state governments, and regulated organizations to provide comprehensive documentation packages that meet specific procurement requirements and timelines.

Most compliance packages are delivered within 48 hours of initial contact, including written attestation letters, technical specifications, and procurement guidance. Contact VDS for NDAA compliance documentation and procurement support.

## Why a plant page

Most security companies do not have a plant. They have a warehouse, a procurement team, and a label-maker. When something fails, the answer is a ticket to a distributor and a four-week lead time on a part that came from someone else's container.

We are not that. This page exists because the difference matters — for compliance, for service, and for the customers who ask, fairly, "where does this come from?"

## What happens at the Pikesville facility

The plant covers chassis integration, electrical assembly, mast and solar mounting, programming and firmware loading, and final QC. Every unit that ships to a customer was on the floor here first.

**Chassis and frame integration.** Trailer chassis arrive from US suppliers. VDS technicians complete the structural integration — mast mounts, equipment bay framing, weatherproofing, and finish work.

**Solar and power systems.** Solar panels are sourced from named NDAA-compliant vendors. Battery banks, charge controllers, and DC distribution are wired and tested on-bench before installation in the unit. Each system is load-tested for the duty cycle it will see in the field.

**Camera and sensor integration.** Cameras (from named NDAA-compliant manufacturers — full list available on request) are mounted, aligned, and weather-sealed. Thermal sensors, radar where specified, and audio deterrents are integrated and bench-tested.

**Programming and platform provisioning.** Each unit is provisioned onto AI VisionStream at the plant. Site templates, alarm zones, and SOC rule sets are pre-loaded. Cellular modems are activated and connectivity verified before shipment.

**Quality control and inspection.** Every unit passes a multi-point inspection: structural, electrical, optical alignment, network handshake to AWS, SOC visibility test, and 72-hour burn-in for solar-power-cycle stability. Inspection records are tied to the unit serial number and retained for the life of the asset.

## In-house vs. sourced

We are honest about what we make and what we buy. The line matters for traceability.

**Done at VDS:** chassis integration, mast assemblies, electrical and DC systems, weatherproofing, programming and firmware, camera mounting and alignment, platform provisioning, QC and burn-in, packaging and shipping.

**Sourced from named vendors:** raw trailer chassis (US suppliers), solar panels (NDAA-compliant US/allied vendors), cameras (named NDAA-compliant manufacturers), batteries (US/allied), cellular modems (US carriers, NDAA-compliant hardware). Vendor list is documented per unit and available to compliance-sensitive customers under NDA.

## Why this matters

**NDAA Section 889 traceability.** Compliance is not a sticker. It is a bill of materials you can defend in front of a federal contracting officer. Because we control assembly, we control the BOM — and we can produce documentation per unit, per serial number, on request.

**Faster service parts.** A camera or power module that fails in Texas does not wait on a container from overseas. Replacements ship from Pikesville, typically same-day or next-day for service-contracted accounts. The same techs who built the unit support it in the field.

**US jobs.** The plant employs technicians, electricians, programmers, and QC inspectors locally. Every unit that ships funds those roles. We are not abstract about this — manufacturing in Maryland is a deliberate choice, and it costs more than offshore assembly. The trade is worth it.

**Iteration speed.** Field feedback loops back into the next production run. When the SOC notices a pattern — a camera angle that creates false alarms, a power profile that fails in shoulder-season cold — engineering changes the next build. Resellers cannot do this. Manufacturers can.

## Visiting the plant

Customers and prospects are welcome to tour the facility. We schedule tours weekly. You will see the floor, meet the team, and watch a unit go through QC. Federal and utility customers conducting compliance audits get a structured walkthrough with documentation.

## Working at the plant

We hire technicians, electricians, network engineers, programmers, and QC inspectors. If you build things with your hands and care that they work in -20F at 3 AM, the roles are open.

h1: Sustainability is an operating cost line. We measure it that way.
heroSubhead: We do not run a corporate ESG program. We run a hardware company that ships solar-powered units because grid hookups cost more than solar arrays. The environmental numbers come out of the operations data.
heroStats: ~4,200 kWh saved per unit per year
body:
A typical jobsite security alternative to a VDS mobile unit is one of two things: a trenched grid hookup with a permanent meter, or a diesel light tower with a 24/7 generator. Both have measurable environmental and economic costs that VDS units avoid by design. This page documents the math.

## The energy baseline

A diesel light tower running surveillance and lighting at a typical construction perimeter consumes approximately 0.6 gallons of diesel per hour. At 24-hour operation, that is 14.4 gallons per day, or roughly 5,250 gallons per year per tower. At current commercial diesel pricing, that is between $20,000 and $25,000 per year per tower in fuel cost alone, plus weekly fuel-delivery truck rolls.

A VDS Sky Guard MSU consumes approximately 11.5 kWh per day under typical 24/7 operation including IR illumination, cellular uplink, edge AI inference, and onboard recording. That energy is supplied by a 1.2 kW solar array with a 25 kWh lithium battery bank sized for 7 days of zero-sun autonomy.

**Fuel consumed per VDS unit per year: zero gallons of diesel.**

## The truck-roll comparison

A diesel tower needs a fuel delivery truck once every 9 to 12 days. Over a 12-month deployment, that is roughly 35 truck rolls per unit, each one with associated emissions and road wear.

A VDS unit needs a service visit on a quarterly maintenance schedule — 4 truck rolls per year for routine inspection, with most service calls handled remotely via the VMS without dispatch. Unplanned site visits average 0.8 per unit per year across the deployed fleet.

**Total truck rolls per VDS unit per year: approximately 5. Reduction versus diesel baseline: 86%.**

## Battery and component lifecycle

The lithium iron phosphate (LiFePO4) battery banks in current VDS units are rated for 6,000+ deep-discharge cycles at 80% depth of discharge. In a typical deployment, that corresponds to a service life of approximately 10–12 years before significant capacity degradation. End-of-life batteries are recycled through partnered LiFePO4 recyclers — not landfilled.

Solar panels are monocrystalline silicon with a 25-year manufacturer warranty and an expected service life of 30 years. Component reuse across unit refurbishment is the standard practice: we have units in field service with panels and battery cells that have been redeployed across three different chassis.

**Comparison:** A grid-tied site requires permanent trenching, conduit, transformers, and metered service. Removing that infrastructure at project end is rare — it usually stays in the ground. Solar units leave no trenching behind.

## Emissions math, on the record

Per unit, per year, against a diesel-tower baseline:

- **Approximately 4,200 kWh** of grid-equivalent or fuel-equivalent energy not consumed
- **Approximately 32 metric tons** of CO2 equivalent not emitted (diesel combustion at 22.4 lbs CO2 per gallon)
- **Approximately 30 fewer truck rolls**, with associated diesel emissions and tire/brake particulate

Across 500+ deployments, the cumulative annual figure is on the order of 16,000 metric tons of CO2e avoided versus the diesel baseline. We do not market against the grid baseline because the comparison is highly site-specific.

## What we do not claim

We do not claim carbon neutrality. We do not buy offsets to pad a marketing number. We do not run a corporate sustainability report with stock photography. The supply chain for solar panels, lithium batteries, and aluminum chassis has its own environmental cost — we are honest about that.

What we claim is a unit-economics-driven product design that happens to produce significantly better environmental outcomes than the alternatives. The customer's accounting team sees this on the operating cost line. The site's environmental compliance team sees it on the air quality and noise reports.

## Noise and light pollution

Diesel towers run at 65–75 dB(A) at 7 meters. VDS units are silent — no rotating machinery, no combustion. IR illumination is invisible to the naked eye and does not contribute to night-sky light pollution. On urban-adjacent and residential-adjacent jobsites, this is a permit and complaint reduction issue, not a marketing claim.

faq.q: What happens to a battery bank at end of life?
faq.a: Returned to VDS, capacity tested, redeployed in lower-duty applications or sent to a partnered LiFePO4 recycler. We track battery serial numbers across deployments.

faq.q: How long does a unit run with no sun at all?
faq.a: 7 days nominal autonomy from a full battery state. In extended overcast scenarios, the system reduces non-essential power draw to extend runtime. We have not had a unit go fully dark on cloud cover alone.

faq.q: Can you provide site-specific energy displacement numbers for a sustainability report?
faq.a: Yes. For deployments over 12 months, we publish energy consumption logs from the VMS that translate directly to displaced-baseline calculations. Contact your account manager.

faq.q: Do you support EPEAT or other green-procurement certifications?
faq.a: Not currently. Our component-level documentation supports most institutional sustainability questionnaires directly without third-party certification.

This page is for the people on your team who ask hard questions before a contract gets signed — IT, security, legal, procurement, and compliance. Each section below is a commitment we will sign in writing.

## 1. Hardware compliance — NDAA Section 889

Every VDS mobile unit shipped since 2022 is fully compliant with the National Defense Authorization Act Section 889 Part A and Part B prohibitions on covered telecommunications equipment. We do not source camera modules, video encoding silicon, or wireless chipsets from any of the five prohibited entities or their subsidiaries.

Our bill-of-materials traceability is reviewed quarterly. We maintain supplier attestations on file for every component. Customers under federal contract or federally-funded grants can request the attestation package via the procurement contact below.

See the dedicated NDAA compliance page for full clause language, prohibited-entity tracking, and our written attestation template.

## 2. Cloud infrastructure — AWS Cloud Partner

The VDS VMS runs on Amazon Web Services in US East (Virginia) and US West (Oregon) regions, with no data replication outside US borders. VDS holds active AWS Cloud Partner status with verified architecture review.

Cloud-side controls in active enforcement:

- **Encryption in transit:** TLS 1.3 on all customer-facing endpoints, certificate-pinned VMS mobile apps, no fallback to TLS 1.1 or earlier.
- **Encryption at rest:** AES-256 on all stored video, metadata, audit logs, and database content, using AWS KMS-managed keys with annual rotation.
- **Network isolation:** Customer tenants are logically isolated. Inter-tenant access is impossible by design — there is no shared schema between customers.
- **Vulnerability management:** Continuous scanning via AWS Inspector and a quarterly third-party penetration test. Latest test report available under NDA.

## 3. Identity, access, and audit

- **Role-Based Access Control (RBAC):** Five role tiers from view-only to global admin. Permissions are inheritable but not transferable. Every role change writes to the audit log.
- **Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA):** TOTP and WebAuthn supported. MFA is enforced for all admin-tier accounts by default and configurable down to view-only by the customer's global admin.
- **SSO:** SAML 2.0 and OIDC supported for enterprise tenants. SCIM provisioning available on the enterprise tier.
- **Audit log:** Every user action, configuration change, video export, and SOC operator interaction is logged with timestamp, user ID, source IP, and result. Logs are immutable and retained for 13 months by default. Longer retention is available by contract.

## 4. Data residency and retention

All customer video, metadata, account data, and audit logs reside in US-based AWS regions. There is no replication to non-US infrastructure for any purpose, including disaster recovery, analytics, or third-party processing.

Default video retention is 30 days hot, 90 days cold-storage. Customer-configurable up to 365 days hot retention. Retention extension does not change data residency — all extended storage remains in US regions.

Customer data is never sold, never licensed, and never used to train external AI models. VDS internal model training uses synthetic and consented data only. This commitment is in every MSA.

## 5. SOC operations and personnel

The VDS Security Operations Center is 100% US-staffed, with operators based in the continental US. There are no offshore monitoring partners, no overnight handoffs to non-US central stations, and no third-party operators with access to customer video.

All SOC operators complete:
- 80-hour initial certification covering escalation protocol, talk-down procedure, and platform operation
- Background check and drug screening (clean current results required)
- Annual recertification with documented competency review
- Quarterly drill participation on simulated P1 events

Average operator tenure as of 2026 is 2.7 years. Operator-to-camera ratio is held below 80:1 during peak hours.

## 6. SOC 2 Type II — in progress

VDS is in active engagement with an independent auditor for SOC 2 Type II certification. Target completion is Q4 2026. The scope includes Security, Availability, and Confidentiality trust service criteria. Customers under enterprise agreement receive interim Type I documentation and direct auditor contact on request.

## 7. Privacy regulations

VDS operates in compliance with applicable US state privacy laws including CCPA (California), CPA (Colorado), VCDPA (Virginia), and successor frameworks as they take effect. We are not a GDPR-scoped controller as our service is US-only. We respond to verified data subject requests within statutory timelines. See the Privacy Policy for the formal mechanism.

## 8. Incident response and disclosure

Material security incidents are disclosed to affected customers within 72 hours of confirmation, in line with industry-standard breach notification practices and applicable state law. We have had zero customer-data security incidents requiring disclosure since founding. We will publish this status on this page if that changes.

heroSubhead: The technical controls that govern how VDS protects video, metadata, customer accounts, and SOC operations against unauthorized access and modification.
body:
## Encryption

### In transit
All traffic between deployed VDS hardware, the AI VisionStream cloud platform, the customer portal, and SOC operator workstations runs over TLS 1.3. We do not accept TLS 1.0 or 1.1 connections at any tier. Cipher suite selection follows current NIST and IETF guidance — forward secrecy is required, RC4 and 3DES are blocked, weak Diffie-Hellman groups are blocked.

Cellular uplink from trailer to AWS ingress uses dual-encryption: the carrier's LTE/5G link encryption plus our application-layer TLS 1.3 wrapper. We do not depend on carrier link encryption alone.

### At rest
All stored video, analytics output, audit log entries, and customer metadata are encrypted at rest with AES-256. Encryption keys are managed in AWS KMS under customer-isolated key hierarchies. Key rotation runs on a defined schedule and on-demand if a compromise is suspected. No customer data sits unencrypted on any VDS-controlled storage at any point.

## Authentication and access control

### Role-based access control (RBAC)
Every customer portal account is assigned a role: Account Owner, Site Manager, Operator, Read-Only, Auditor. Each role maps to a defined permission set covering camera access, alert acknowledgement, video export, user management, and audit log visibility. Roles are configured by the customer's Account Owner — VDS does not assign portal roles inside customer tenants.

### Multi-factor authentication (MFA)
MFA is required for all administrative roles and available for all roles. TOTP (Google Authenticator, Authy, 1Password) is supported standard. WebAuthn / FIDO2 hardware keys are supported and recommended for Account Owner accounts.

### Single sign-on
Enterprise customers can federate the VDS portal to their identity provider via SAML 2.0 or OpenID Connect. We have completed integrations with Okta, Microsoft Entra ID, Google Workspace, Ping Identity, and JumpCloud. Just-in-time provisioning and SCIM user lifecycle management are supported on enterprise plans.

### IP allowlisting
Customer portal access can be restricted to defined IP ranges or CIDR blocks at the tenant level. SOC operator access is always restricted to VDS-managed network egress; we do not allow SOC operations from arbitrary IPs.

## Audit log

Every authentication event, configuration change, video access event, alert acknowledgement, and administrative action is written to an immutable audit log retained for 12 months minimum. The log is append-only — there is no operator function that can edit or delete entries.

Customers can export the audit log to CSV or stream it via webhook to a SIEM. We have customers feeding the log into Splunk, Datadog, and Microsoft Sentinel.

## Penetration testing

VDS contracts an independent third-party penetration test annually, covering the AI VisionStream cloud platform, customer portal, mobile applications, and deployed trailer ingress. Test methodology follows OWASP ASVS Level 2 minimum and NIST SP 800-115 process guidelines. The most recent test was completed in Q4 2025; the next is scheduled for Q4 2026.

Findings are remediated on a severity-based schedule: critical findings within 7 days, high within 30, medium within 90. The summary report is available under NDA to enterprise customers' security teams.

## Vulnerability disclosure

VDS operates a responsible-disclosure program for security researchers. Reports route to security@visiondetectionsystems.com with PGP encryption supported. We acknowledge inbound reports within two business days, triage to a severity within five, and commit to coordinated disclosure on a timeline appropriate to the finding.

We do not currently operate a paid bug bounty. We do credit researchers on a Hall of Fame page when they request public acknowledgement and the report meets quality criteria.

## Hardware and field operations

Deployed trailers run a hardened Linux operating system. Remote SSH is disabled by default; out-of-band management runs through a dedicated, mutually-authenticated channel. Firmware updates are signed, verified, and applied during defined maintenance windows. We do not push unsigned firmware. Ever.

Trailers do not store customer video locally beyond a short rolling buffer; primary storage is cloud-side under AWS US-only regions.

body:
## Where customer data lives

All VDS customer data — video, analytics output, audit logs, account metadata — is stored exclusively in AWS US-East and US-West regions. We do not replicate, mirror, or back up customer data to any non-US AWS region or any non-AWS infrastructure.

This is a contractual commitment, not a default that can drift. The AWS account configuration enforces region restriction at the IAM and bucket policy level. A misconfigured deployment cannot accidentally land data outside the US footprint.

## Tenant isolation

Each customer operates in a logically isolated tenant. Customer A's video, analytics, and metadata are not accessible to Customer B's portal users, Customer B's SOC dashboards, or Customer B's API tokens — ever. Tenant boundaries are enforced at the application layer, the database layer (row-level security on shared tables, customer-specific keys on object storage), and the audit layer.

VDS internal personnel access to customer data is limited to SOC operators handling active alerts and the small set of platform engineering staff who maintain the underlying infrastructure. Every internal access event is logged to the customer's audit log if it touches their tenant.

## What VDS does not do with customer data

We do not share customer video, analytics output, or metadata with any third party without explicit customer authorization. This includes:

- We do not sell or license customer data for analytics, training, or any other secondary purpose
- We do not aggregate identifiable customer footage into training datasets for our AI VisionStream models — model training uses synthetic and licensed datasets
- We do not provide customer data to law enforcement absent a valid subpoena, court order, or customer authorization (and we notify the customer when we receive such a request unless legally prohibited)
- We do not use customer video for marketing, case studies, or promotional materials without an executed release

## Biometrics, facial recognition, and BIPA

VDS AI VisionStream performs object detection (person, vehicle), license plate recognition (LPR), behavior analytics (loitering, perimeter breach), and scene classification. It does not perform facial recognition, biometric identification, or biometric template generation.

This is a deliberate product position. It keeps VDS clear of Illinois BIPA exposure, Texas CUBI exposure, Washington WBPA exposure, and the patchwork of city-level facial recognition bans (Portland OR, San Francisco, Boston, others). It also reflects an operating principle: license plates and behavior patterns are tools we need, biometric identification is not.

If a customer requests facial recognition as a feature, the answer is no. We will not add it.

## CCPA, GDPR, and regulatory posture

### California (CCPA / CPRA)
VDS treats CCPA as a baseline for all US customers regardless of state. We honor verifiable consumer requests for access, deletion, and correction. We do not sell personal information as defined under CCPA. Service provider agreements are in place with all sub-processors.

### Other state privacy laws
VDS complies with comparable state privacy regimes including VCDPA (Virginia), CPA (Colorado), CTDPA (Connecticut), UCPA (Utah), and others as they come into force. We track the state-by-state landscape and update our practices ahead of effective dates.

### GDPR-adjacent practices
VDS does not currently offer services to EU-resident customers, but we follow GDPR-adjacent principles — purpose limitation, data minimization, lawful basis documentation, breach notification timelines — as a baseline. If you are a US-based enterprise with EU operations and need GDPR-equivalent documentation for a global program, talk to us.

## Retention and deletion

### Default retention
Video and analytics data: 30, 60, or 90 days based on customer plan. Audit logs: 12 months minimum, longer on enterprise plans or by contract. Account metadata: retained for the duration of the customer relationship plus the regulatory hold period.

### Customer-initiated deletion
Customers can request deletion of specific video segments, full site data, or full account data at any time. Deletion executes within 30 days, with cryptographic destruction of the underlying encryption keys to render any residual storage unrecoverable.

### Contract termination
On termination, customer data is exportable for 60 days. After 60 days, all customer data is purged from primary and backup storage within 30 additional days. Termination data destruction is logged and a destruction certificate provided on request.

heroSubhead: The service commitments VDS makes operationally and contractually — platform uptime, SOC response, hardware response, and what happens when we miss.
body:
## Platform availability

### Target: 99.9% monthly uptime
AI VisionStream cloud platform — the camera-agnostic VMS, analytics processing, customer portal, and API — runs to a 99.9% monthly uptime target measured against the customer portal availability endpoint.

99.9% per calendar month allows a maximum of approximately 43 minutes of accumulated downtime. Scheduled maintenance windows announced 7+ days in advance are excluded from the calculation; emergency maintenance is included.

### Measurement
Uptime is measured by an external synthetic monitor running from three geographically separated AWS regions at one-minute intervals. The public status page shows real-time and historical uptime against the SLA target. Customers receive monthly uptime reports automatically on enterprise plans; available on request on standard plans.

## SOC response

### Target: <60 seconds alert acknowledgement
Every AI VisionStream alert routed to the SOC is acknowledged by a live US-based operator in under 60 seconds, measured from alert arrival at the SOC queue to operator acknowledgement. This is the SOC's single most-tracked operational metric.

2025 full-year median: 14 seconds. 95th percentile: 38 seconds. 99th percentile: 71 seconds. The handful of >60-second events are post-incident reviewed and root-caused.

### Escalation timing
After acknowledgement, the operator follows the customer's defined escalation tree: video verification, audio talk-down where authorized, on-site contact notification, and law enforcement dispatch when criteria are met. Escalation timing depends on the action — talk-down is typically inside two minutes of alert, LE dispatch is a function of how fast PSAP answers.

## Hardware response

### Mean-time-to-respond (MTTR) on field issues
For trailer hardware issues — sensor fault, cellular degradation, solar performance, physical damage — VDS targets:

- **Critical (unit offline):** Remote diagnosis inside 2 hours, field response inside 24 hours
- **Major (degraded operation):** Remote diagnosis inside 4 business hours, field response inside 72 hours
- **Minor (non-impacting fault):** Remote diagnosis next business day, field response inside 10 business days

MTTR is measured from customer ticket open to issue resolution in the customer portal. Reported monthly on enterprise plans.

## Credit policy

### Platform uptime miss
If AI VisionStream monthly uptime falls below the 99.9% target, customers receive a service credit calculated against the affected service month:

- 99.0% - 99.9% uptime: 10% credit
- 95.0% - 98.99% uptime: 25% credit
- Below 95.0% uptime: 50% credit

Credits are applied to the following month's invoice automatically — no claim form required on enterprise plans. Standard plan credits are filed via support ticket.

### SOC response SLA miss
If SOC median monthly response exceeds the 60-second target, affected customers receive a 10% credit of the SOC service component for that month. Per-incident credits for individual late responses are not standard; pattern misses trigger the credit.

### Hardware response SLA miss
Hardware response misses are credited per-incident under enterprise plans; standard plan hardware response is best-effort against published targets.

## What's excluded from SLA

Following industry standard:

- Force majeure events (natural disasters, regional carrier outages outside our control)
- Customer-caused issues (network changes, account misconfiguration, denial of cellular service at the carrier level)
- Scheduled maintenance announced 7+ days in advance
- Beta or pilot features explicitly designated as not under SLA

faq.a: status.visiondetectionsystems.com — link in this page footer. Subscribe by email or RSS for incident notifications.

faq.q: How is the 60-second SOC target measured?
faq.a: Time from alert arrival at the SOC queue to live operator acknowledgement, captured in the SOC tooling and audited monthly.

faq.q: Can I get a higher uptime commitment on enterprise plans?
faq.a: 99.95% is available on enterprise plans by contract amendment. The underlying architecture supports it; the elevated target reflects different credit math and is priced accordingly.

faq.q: What counts as an incident?
faq.a: Any unplanned event that degrades or interrupts platform availability or SOC operations affecting one or more customers. Posted to the status page within 15 minutes of detection.

VDS is an Amazon Web Services Cloud Partner. AI VisionStream runs on AWS US regions exclusively, and the partnership designation reflects validated technical alignment with AWS architectural best practices, security controls, and data residency commitments.

For enterprise customers running AWS at scale internally, partner status simplifies vendor-to-vendor due diligence — your team can verify our AWS posture through AWS's own partner channels.

VDS hardware and operational stack comply with National Defense Authorization Act Section 889(a)(1)(A) and 889(a)(1)(B). Attestation documentation is available for federal contractors, defense suppliers, grant-funded programs, and any prime contractor requiring 889 representations from their vendors.

This is not a marketing claim — it's a documented attestation, refreshed annually and tied to specific hardware bills-of-materials and operational architecture.

VDS hardware is also compliant with state-level procurement restrictions on specific Chinese-manufactured camera brands (Hikvision, Dahua) that exist in Florida, Texas, Georgia, and other states. VDS work has been referenced in industry publications covering construction security, mobile surveillance technology, and physical security operations. Specific press mention list is maintained on the press kit page and refreshed as new coverage publishes.
